paras.text: … the resulting high levels of glucose in the blood and the inadequate amount of glucose in the cells together produce the symptoms and complications of diabetes. Diabetes mellitus is a disorder in which the amount of sugar in the blood is elevated. Doctors often use the full name diabetes mellitus, rather than diabetes alone, to distinguish this disorder from diabetes insipidus.

paras.text: Diabetes mellitus is a disorder in which blood sugar (glucose) levels are abnormally high because the body does not produce enough insulin to meet its needs.

paras.text: Diabetes insipidus is a relatively rare disorder that does not affect blood glucose levels but, just like diabetes mellitus, also causes increased urination.

paras.text: Lipids perform a number of different functions in living organisms. Some of these are listed below.
paras.urdu: لپڈز جانداروں میں کئی مختلف افعال انجام دیتے ہیں۔ ان میں سے چند نیچے درج ہیں۔

paras.text: Lipids provide food, which is highly rich in calorific value. One gram of lipid on complete oxidation produces 9.3 kcal of heat, which is about double the amount produced by carbohydrates and proteins.
paras.urdu: لپڈز ایسی خوراک مہیا کرتے ہیں جو حرارتی قدر میں بہت بھرپور ہے۔ ایک گرام لپڈ کی مکمل تکسید سے 9.3 kcal حرارت پیدا ہوتی ہے، جو کاربوہائیڈریٹس اور پروٹینز سے پیدا ہونے والی مقدار کا تقریباً دوگنا ہے۔

paras.text: Lipids are insoluble in water and, therefore, they can be stored easily in the body as food reserves. The organisms then use these food reserves during hibernation periods.
paras.urdu: لپڈز پانی میں ناحل پذیر ہیں اس لیے انہیں جسم میں خوراک کے ذخیرے کے طور پر آسانی سے محفوظ کیا جا سکتا ہے۔ پھر جاندار سرمائی نیند کے دوران یہ ذخیرے استعمال کرتے ہیں۔

paras.text: Lipids in association with different proteins form the important constituents of cell membranes.
paras.urdu: لپڈز مختلف پروٹینز کے ساتھ مل کر خلوی جھلیوں کے اہم اجزا بناتے ہیں۔

paras.text: Fats have high insulating capacity. Great quantities of fats are deposited in the sub-cutaneous layers in aquatic mammals such as whale and in animals of cold climates. These fat deposits protect these animals from severe cold and severe temperature changes.

paras.text: 21.5 Nucleic Acids

paras.text: Nucleic acids are macromolecules that allow organisms to transfer genetic information from one generation to the next. They are present in every living organism as well as viruses. They have been found to be the essential substance of the genes and the apparatus by which the genes act or express themselves. They contain in their structure the blueprints for the normal growth and development of each and every organism
paras.urdu: نیوکلک ایسڈز وہ بڑے سالمات ہیں جو جانداروں کو جینیاتی معلومات ایک نسل سے اگلی نسل میں منتقل کرنے کے قابل بناتے ہیں۔ یہ ہر جاندار اور وائرسوں میں موجود ہیں۔ یہ جینز کا بنیادی مادہ اور وہ آلہ پائے گئے ہیں جس سے جینز عمل کرتے یا خود کو ظاہر کرتے ہیں۔ ان کی ساخت میں ہر جاندار کی معمول کی نشوونما اور ترقی کے خاکے ہوتے ہیں
paras.pashto: نیوکلیک اسیدونه هغه لوی مالیکولونه دي چې ژوندیو موجوداتو ته اجازه ورکوي جنیټیکي معلومات له یوه نسل څخه بل ته ولېږدوي. په هر ژوندي موجود او ویروسونو کې شته. موندل شوي چې د جینونو اساسي ماده او هغه وسیله ده چې جینونه پرې عمل کوي یا ځان څرګندوي. په خپل جوړښت کې د هر ژوندي موجود د عادي ودې او پرمختګ نقشې لري

paras.text: Nucleic acids are the main information-carrying molecules of the cell, and, by directing the process of protein synthesis, they determine the inherited characteristics of every living thing.
paras.urdu: نیوکلک ایسڈز خلیے کے معلومات لے جانے والے اہم سالمات ہیں، اور پروٹین کی تالیف کے عمل کی رہنمائی کر کے یہ ہر جاندار کی موروثی خصوصیات متعین کرتے ہیں۔

paras.text: The two main classes of nucleic acids are deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and ribonucleic acid (RNA).
paras.urdu: نیوکلک ایسڈز کی دو بڑی جماعتیں ڈی آکسی رائبونیوکلک ایسڈ (DNA) اور رائبونیوکلک ایسڈ (RNA) ہیں۔

paras.text: DNA is the genetic material found in living organisms, from single-celled bacteria to multicellular mammals.
paras.urdu: DNA وہ جینیاتی مادہ ہے جو یک خلوی بیکٹیریا سے کثیر خلوی ممالیہ تک جانداروں میں پایا جاتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: DNA هغه جنیټیکي ماده ده چې له یو حجروي باکتریاوو تر څو حجروي تي لرونکو پورې په ژوندیو موجوداتو کې موندل کېږي.

paras.text: RNA is the genetic material of certain viruses, but it is also found in all living cells, where it plays an important role in certain processes such as the synthesis of proteins.
paras.urdu: RNA بعض وائرسوں کا جینیاتی مادہ ہے، لیکن یہ تمام زندہ خلیوں میں بھی پایا جاتا ہے جہاں یہ پروٹینز کی تالیف جیسے بعض عمل میں اہم کردار ادا کرتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: RNA د ځینو ویروسونو جنیټیکي ماده ده، خو په ټولو ژوندیو حجرو کې هم موندل کېږي چې پکې په ځینو عملیو لکه د پروټینونو په جوړولو کې مهم رول لوبوي.

paras.text: They are capable of being broken down to yield phosphoric acid, sugars, and a mixture of organic bases (purines and pyrimidines).
paras.urdu: انہیں توڑ کر فاسفورک ایسڈ، شکر اور نامیاتی اساسوں (پیورینز اور پیریمیڈینز) کا آمیزہ حاصل کیا جا سکتا ہے۔

paras.text: Nucleic acids are substances present in the nuclei of cells which are involved in the storage, expressing, transmission and processing of genetic information and mutation in living organisms. The monomer that makes up a nucleic acid is called a nucleotide.
paras.urdu: نیوکلک ایسڈز خلیوں کے مرکزوں میں موجود وہ مادے ہیں جو جانداروں میں جینیاتی معلومات کے ذخیرے، اظہار، منتقلی اور عمل کاری اور تغیر میں شامل ہیں۔ نیوکلک ایسڈ بنانے والے مونومر کو نیوکلیوٹائیڈ کہتے ہیں۔
paras.pashto: نیوکلیک اسیدونه د حجرو په هستو کې شته هغه مواد دي چې په ژوندیو موجوداتو کې د جنیټیکي معلوماتو په زېرمه کولو، څرګندولو، لېږد او پروسس او بدلون (میوټېشن) کې ونډه لري. هغه مونومر چې نیوکلیک اسید جوړوي نیوکلیوټایډ بلل کېږي.

paras.text: 21.5.1 Structural Components of DNA and RNA

paras.text: Watson and Crick determined the structure of nucleic acids. Both DNA and RNA are formed by the polymerization of large number of units known as nucleotides. That is why DNA and RNA are polynucleotides. A nucleotide is composed of a nitrogenous base, a sugar and a phosphate group. DNA differs from RNA in the type of nitrogenous base and type of sugar unit. The nitrogenous bases are of two types, purine and pyrimidine.
paras.urdu: واٹسن اور کرک نے نیوکلک ایسڈز کی ساخت متعین کی۔ DNA اور RNA دونوں نیوکلیوٹائیڈز کہلانے والی بڑی تعداد میں اکائیوں کی پولیمرائزیشن سے بنتے ہیں۔ اسی لیے DNA اور RNA پولی نیوکلیوٹائیڈز ہیں۔ نیوکلیوٹائیڈ ایک نائٹروجنی اساس، ایک شکر اور ایک فاسفیٹ گروپ پر مشتمل ہے۔ DNA نائٹروجنی اساس کی قسم اور شکر کی اکائی کی قسم میں RNA سے مختلف ہے۔ نائٹروجنی اساس دو قسم کے ہیں، پیورین اور پیریمیڈین۔

DNA د نایټروجني قلوي د ډول او د بورې د واحد د ډول له مخې له RNA توپیر لري. نایټروجني قلوي دوه ډوله دي، پیورین او پیریمیډین.

sections.theory:
… the resulting high levels of glucose in the blood and the inadequate amount of glucose in the cells together produce the symptoms and complications of diabetes. Diabetes mellitus is a disorder in which the amount of sugar in the blood is elevated. Doctors often use the full name diabetes mellitus, rather than diabetes alone, to distinguish this disorder from diabetes insipidus.

Diabetes mellitus is a disorder in which blood sugar (glucose) levels are abnormally high because the body does not produce enough insulin to meet its needs.

Diabetes insipidus is a relatively rare disorder that does not affect blood glucose levels but, just like diabetes mellitus, also causes increased urination.

21.4.4 Nutritional and Biological Importance of lipids

Lipids perform a number of different functions in living organisms. Some of these are listed below.

Lipids provide food, which is highly rich in calorific value. One gram of lipid on complete oxidation produces 9.3 kcal of heat, which is about double the amount produced by carbohydrates and proteins.

Lipids are insoluble in water and, therefore, they can be stored easily in the body as food reserves. The organisms then use these food reserves during hibernation periods.

Lipids in association with different proteins form the important constituents of cell membranes.

Fats have high insulating capacity. Great quantities of fats are deposited in the sub-cutaneous layers in aquatic mammals such as whale and in animals of cold climates. These fat deposits protect these animals from severe cold and severe temperature changes.

Some lipids especially phospholipids play a key role in the absorption and transportation of fatty acids in the body.

Sex hormones, adrenocorticoids, cholic acids are synthesized from a steroidal lipid known as cholesterol.

Lipids serve as carrier of fats soluble vitamins such as vitamin A, D and E in the body.

Squealing, a steroid present in the blood of shark has antibiotic and antifungal properties. This explains why sharks rarely contract infections and almost never get cancer.

21.5 Nucleic Acids

Nucleic acids are macromolecules that allow organisms to transfer genetic information from one generation to the next. They are present in every living organism as well as viruses. They have been found to be the essential substance of the genes and the apparatus by which the genes act or express themselves. They contain in their structure the blueprints for the normal growth and development of each and every organism

Nucleic acids are the main information-carrying molecules of the cell, and, by directing the process of protein synthesis, they determine the inherited characteristics of every living thing.

The two main classes of nucleic acids are deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and ribonucleic acid (RNA).

DNA is the genetic material found in living organisms, from single-celled bacteria to multicellular mammals.

RNA is the genetic material of certain viruses, but it is also found in all living cells, where it plays an important role in certain processes such as the synthesis of proteins.

They are capable of being broken down to yield phosphoric acid, sugars, and a mixture of organic bases (purines and pyrimidines).

Nucleic acids are substances present in the nuclei of cells which are involved in the storage, expressing, transmission and processing of genetic information and mutation in living organisms. The monomer that makes up a nucleic acid is called a nucleotide.

Types of Nucleic Acids

There are two types of nucleic acids.

DNA (Deoxyribonucleic acid) it is present in nuclei and in some viruses. It is the main constituent of chromosome.

RNA (Ribonucleic acid) is present in the cytoplasm and in some viruses.

21.5.1 Structural Components of DNA and RNA

Watson and Crick determined the structure of nucleic acids. Both DNA and RNA are formed by the polymerization of large number of units known as nucleotides. That is why DNA and RNA are polynucleotides. A nucleotide is composed of a nitrogenous base, a sugar and a phosphate group. DNA differs from RNA in the type of nitrogenous base and type of sugar unit. The nitrogenous bases are of two types, purine and pyrimidine.

… the resulting high levels of glucose in the blood and the inadequate amount of glucose in the cells together produce the symptoms and complications of diabetes. Diabetes mellitus is a disorder in which the amount of sugar in the blood is elevated. Doctors often use the full name diabetes mellitus, rather than diabetes alone, to distinguish this disorder from diabetes insipidus.

Diabetes mellitus is a disorder in which blood sugar (glucose) levels are abnormally high because the body does not produce enough insulin to meet its needs.

Diabetes insipidus is a relatively rare disorder that does not affect blood glucose levels but, just like diabetes mellitus, also causes increased urination.

21.4.4 Nutritional and Biological Importance of lipids

Lipids perform a number of different functions in living organisms. Some of these are listed below.

Lipids provide food, which is highly rich in calorific value. One gram of lipid on complete oxidation produces 9.3 kcal of heat, which is about double the amount produced by carbohydrates and proteins.

Lipids are insoluble in water and, therefore, they can be stored easily in the body as food reserves. The organisms then use these food reserves during hibernation periods.

Lipids in association with different proteins form the important constituents of cell membranes.

Fats have high insulating capacity. Great quantities of fats are deposited in the sub-cutaneous layers in aquatic mammals such as whale and in animals of cold climates. These fat deposits protect these animals from severe cold and severe temperature changes.

Some lipids especially phospholipids play a key role in the absorption and transportation of fatty acids in the body.

Sex hormones, adrenocorticoids, cholic acids are synthesized from a steroidal lipid known as cholesterol.

Lipids serve as carrier of fats soluble vitamins such as vitamin A, D and E in the body.

Squealing, a steroid present in the blood of shark has antibiotic and antifungal properties. This explains why sharks rarely contract infections and almost never get cancer.

21.5 Nucleic Acids

Nucleic acids are macromolecules that allow organisms to transfer genetic information from one generation to the next. They are present in every living organism as well as viruses. They have been found to be the essential substance of the genes and the apparatus by which the genes act or express themselves. They contain in their structure the blueprints for the normal growth and development of each and every organism

Nucleic acids are the main information-carrying molecules of the cell, and, by directing the process of protein synthesis, they determine the inherited characteristics of every living thing.

The two main classes of nucleic acids are deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and ribonucleic acid (RNA).

DNA is the genetic material found in living organisms, from single-celled bacteria to multicellular mammals.

RNA is the genetic material of certain viruses, but it is also found in all living cells, where it plays an important role in certain processes such as the synthesis of proteins.

They are capable of being broken down to yield phosphoric acid, sugars, and a mixture of organic bases (purines and pyrimidines).

Nucleic acids are substances present in the nuclei of cells which are involved in the storage, expressing, transmission and processing of genetic information and mutation in living organisms. The monomer that makes up a nucleic acid is called a nucleotide.

Types of Nucleic Acids

There are two types of nucleic acids.

DNA (Deoxyribonucleic acid) it is present in nuclei and in some viruses. It is the main constituent of chromosome.

RNA (Ribonucleic acid) is present in the cytoplasm and in some viruses.

21.5.1 Structural Components of DNA and RNA

Watson and Crick determined the structure of nucleic acids. Both DNA and RNA are formed by the polymerization of large number of units known as nucleotides. That is why DNA and RNA are polynucleotides. A nucleotide is composed of a nitrogenous base, a sugar and a phosphate group. DNA differs from RNA in the type of nitrogenous base and type of sugar unit. The nitrogenous bases are of two types, purine and pyrimidine.
